items.body: Gang of Four, the English post-punk band from Leeds, released their debut album “Entertainment!” on 25 September 1979 through EMI, with Warner Bros. Records handling North America. The album turns 47 this year. It runs 39 minutes and 53 seconds across twelve tracks and was recorded that same year at The Workhouse on the Old Kent Road in London. Jon King and Andy Gill produced it with the band’s then-manager Rob Warr, and Rik Walton engineered. The line-up was King on lead vocals, percussion and melodica, Gill on electric guitar and vocals, Dave Allen on bass and Hugo Burnham on drums. EMI had signed the group after its debut release, the three-track “Damaged Goods” EP, issued on 13 October 1978 by Bob Last’s Edinburgh label Fast Product and recorded at Cargo Studios in Rochdale. Two of those three tracks, “Damaged Goods” and “Love Like Anthrax”, were re-recorded for the album. The running order is “Ether”, “Natural’s Not in It”, “Not Great Men”, “Damaged Goods”, “Return the Gift”, “Guns Before Butter”, “I Found That Essence Rare”, “Glass”, “Contract”, “At Home He’s a Tourist”, “5.45” and “Love Like Anthrax”. King wrote the lyrics under the influence of Situationism, the writing of Michel Foucault and Jacques Lacan, feminism and Marx’s theory of alienation. He also designed the sleeve, which reproduces a still from a Winnetou film in three processed versions, with a text reading: “The Indian smiles, he thinks that the cowboy is his friend. The cowboy smiles, he is glad the Indian is fooled. Now he can exploit him.” “At Home He’s a Tourist” reached number 58 in the UK Singles Chart, still the highest placing of any Gang of Four song. The band were booked to perform it on Top of the Pops, but the producers asked them to change the line “and the rubbers you hide in your top left pocket” to “rubbish”; the group refused and the appearance was cancelled. The album peaked at number 45 on the UK Albums Chart and number 35 in New Zealand. Writing in Rolling Stone in August 1980, David Fricke called it “the best debut album by a British band – punk or otherwise – since the original English release of The Clash”. About Gang of Four Gang of Four formed in Leeds in 1976 around guitarist Andy Gill and singer Jon King, who had met as students. Drummer Hugo Burnham and bassist Dave Wolfson completed the first line-up; after two or three gigs Wolfson was replaced by Dave Allen in 1977. Fast Product released the “Damaged Goods” EP in October 1978, and EMI signed the band the following year. “Entertainment!” arrived in September 1979 and was followed by “Solid Gold” in March 1981 and “Songs of the Free” in 1982, the latter carrying “I Love a Man in Uniform”, which was dropped from BBC playlists during the Falklands conflict. Allen left in 1981 after two albums and went on to co-found Shriekback; Busta “Cherry” Jones filled in before Sara Lee joined as the permanent bassist. Burnham left in 1982 and Steve Goulding took over the drum stool for “Hard” (1983). The band split in 1984. Gill and King reconvened three times in the 1990s, recording “Mall” (1991) with Gail Ann Dorsey on bass and “Shrinkwrapped” (1995). The founding four reunited in 2004 and toured the UK in 2005, releasing the re-recorded “Return the Gift” on 28 September 2005 and performing “Entertainment!” in full for the All Tomorrow’s Parties Don’t Look Back series that year; Side-Line covered the band’s later live material in Exclusive preview Gang Of Four’s ‘Live…In The Moment’ live album. Burnham departed again in late 2005 to return to teaching, and Allen was replaced by Thomas McNeice in 2008. King left in 2011 after disagreements with Gill, and John Sterry took over vocals. That line-up issued “Content” (2011), “What Happens Next” (2015) and “Happy Now” (2019). Andy Gill died on 1 February 2020, aged 64, ending that incarnation of the band. In October 2021 King reformed Gang of Four with Burnham, Sara Lee and Slint guitarist David Pajo for a tour of 1977 to 1983 material. Lee was replaced by Linda Pardee in January 2024 and then by Gail Greenwood that July, and Pajo by Ted Leo in January 2025. Dave Allen died in April 2025, aged 69, having lived with early-onset dementia. The band played its final show in Amsterdam on 6 July 2025. The record’s reach outlasted the band. Die Krupps recorded a version of “To Hell With Poverty” for their 2021 covers album, as reported in Die Krupps cover Gang Of Four with new single ‘To Hell With Poverty’. Michael Stipe has said of the band: “Gang of Four could really swing. I stole a lot from them.” Rolling Stone placed “Entertainment!” at number 490 on its 500 Greatest Albums list in 2003, number 483 in 2012 and number 273 in 2020, and Kevin J. H. Dettmar wrote a book on it for the 33 1/3 series in 2014. Forty-seven years on, the debut remains the album on which the Leeds four-piece set its guitar, bass and drums against lyrics about commodities, contracts and the news.
items._cn_summary: 这张1979年的首张专辑将放克节奏与尖锐吉他切入马克思主义、情境主义、福柯与拉康的文本框架，形成去旋律化、以律动和思想性驱动的结构。歌词由Jon King撰写，Andy Gill的吉他采用金属化、棱角分明的切分处理，鼓与贝斯构成几乎机械化的律动骨架，与当时多数朋克乐队截然不同。封面引用西部片静帧配以殖民剥削的旁白，视觉与文本层面均延续了对消费主义与意识形态的拆解。曲目如《Damaged Goods》《At Home He's a Tourist》以极少乐句反复推进，录音在伦敦The Workhouse完成，时长不到四十分钟，是后朋克场景中将理论文本转化为音乐语汇的早期范例，也是对主流流行娱乐概念的直接对抗。

items.body: Top PickThe Ocean – Solaris (progressive post-metal) Eden should be along with a proper review sometime in the near future, but it's safe to say this first outing from the new Ocean line-up is not only a bona fide success, but also stands out as one of their strongest albums to date. The jump in quality might not come as a surprise after the snoozefest that was Holoxene (2023), but there's an argument to be made that this is the best Ocean album since genuine GOAT-contender Pelagial (2013), or even outside of it.At well over an hour and with songs and song-suites pushing the ten, fifteen and even twenty-minute mark, Solaris can be a tall order. Likewise, its expansive and layered composition works best when played in full and paying it complete attention, which is probably why I haven't listened to it nearly as much as I should have, even though we've had the promo for a month or so now. Rest assured though, that this is an album I will be playing and referring back to for years to come, and I doubt I'm alone in that assessment. Solaris by The Ocean Last Week's Most Unjustifiably Overlooked ReleaseUncle Acid and the Deadbeats – Shapes of Midnight (occult rock/metal)I didn't give this one a proper listen before posting last week's roundup, we got the promo early, but, after a quick sample I wrote it off as a good album from a band I respected but traditionally Wasn't For Me™. I should have paid more heed to Jordan's review though, because—while I'm not qualified to comment on whether this is the best Uncle Acid and the Deadbeats album—I can say its doing a whole lot more for me than any of their previous records have, or similar releases of its ilk have been lately.In comparison to the shark-jumping self-parody of the new Green Lung record, Shapes of Midnight oozes class and sincerity, along with a compelling mastery of its craft. It also rocks super hard. Along with the expected malaize of psychedelic Black Sabbath worship that pervades their sound, "Psycho on the Loose" sounds like Turbonegro covering Turbo-era Judas Priest, while "Don't Let it Control You" almost sounds like Motorhead mixed with Hellhammer, with lots of bass fills that bring to mind "Born to Be Wild". Indeed, bassist Justin Smith may well be the man of the match, delivering a Meddle-esque Pink Floyd trudge on "When Evil Wakes" and plenty of Geezer Butler-isms throughout that help make Shapes of Midnight a surprisingly vital pre-summer soundtrack as the weather starts to get warmer down under. items._cn_summary: 本期精选聚焦两张专辑：The Ocean 新作延续渐进后金属路线，曲目时长跨度大，从十分钟到二十分钟不等，编曲层次繁复，需完整专注聆听，整体质量被视为乐队近年最佳之一。Uncle Acid and the Deadbeats 的《Shapes of Midnight》被定位为神秘摇滚/金属方向，融合了迷幻黑安息山崇拜的元素，贝斯线条突出，呈现出沉稳有质感的复古摇滚气质。文中还列举了大量其他新发行作品，涵盖葬礼末日、工业黑金属、交响金属、噪音摇滚等多种风格，信息密度较高但大多为简要罗列。整体乐评以重金属及其子类型为主，与实验、前卫、电子、暗潮等偏好领域的交集有限，仅 The Ocean 的渐进金属在'前卫'维度上有部分契合。

items._cn_summary: 须川崇志、林正樹、石若骏组成的Banksia Trio推出新作《The Great Noon》，此前已完成欧洲巡演，被定位为全球乐迷值得关注的新一代钢琴三重奏。整张专辑以林正樹的钢琴为核心，他的旋律时而如画面般展开，时而腾空跃动、变化莫测，展现出作为剧伴作曲家的叙事能力。石若骏的鼓击在细腻触感与爆发力之间游走，曾活跃于从富士摇滚到红白歌合战等不同舞台。须川崇志的低音贝斯提供深沉音色与丰富声响变化，作为三人架构的根基。专辑标题与整体氛围暗示着一种明亮而饱满的声响世界，但乐评中并未深入探讨具体的实验性手法或突破性元素，更偏向于对三位成员既有技艺的整合与展示。

items._cn_summary: 贝斯手兼作曲家Max Johnson发起众筹，计划发行五张专辑，涵盖作曲与即兴两大方向。其中包括与Anna Webber和Michael Sarin合作的三重奏作品，基于2022至2023年的巡演素材；另有一张与Nate Wooley及Brian共同完成的即兴与重构组曲，主题围绕疫情期间的停滞感与社交距离展开。从已披露的阵容与合作方式来看，这些项目延续了当代纽约即兴音乐圈的创作脉络，将原声乐器置于开放的结构框架内，允许演奏者在预设素材与自由对话之间游走。五张专辑的集群式发行策略本身就具有策展意味，试图呈现一位贝斯手在不同编制下的多面向探索。

items.body: Columbus’s Pinta, Niña and Santa María sail through “Delfín del Mundo” alongside pineapples, cockerels, chocolate, tobacco and caipirinhas, a roll call of conquest and tropical produce chanted over a psychedelic cumbia. “Delfín del Mundo” is the third and final single from Desertropical, the new EP from Dr. Rayo, due in October on Costa Rican label Lácteo Cósmico. The project belongs to Red Jesus, a Chilean-Mexican percussionist and producer who spent 2014 to 2020 on Mexico’s independent circuit. Now based in Madrid, he launched the project with a sold-out night at Moby Dick. Red Jesus made the track with Barzo, the San José-born DJ and producer who runs Lácteo Cósmico and has remixed Janelle Monáe and Erykah Badu. He came to Madrid for a short visit, and the pair recorded most of the instruments live at Dr. Rayo’s base. Barzo then built the electronic production on top of those takes. The earlier singles “Mexicali Tropical” and “Owl on Cocaine” opened big and dramatic, while “Delfín del Mundo” settles into a mid-tempo sway built on a slow-burning bassline, live percussion and a vocal delivered close to a chant. The vocal carries a message of pride in Latin American roots, and the cacao, tobacco and pineapples in the lyric were growing in the Americas long before Columbus’s ships arrived. Desertropical gets a launch party at Madrid’s Siroco at the end of September, with Spanish dates to follow in Seville, Oviedo, Gijón, Logroño and Santander. Stream “Delfín del Mundo” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Dr. Rayo x Barzo – Delfín del Mundo appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 《Delfín del Mundo》是Dr. Rayo与Barzo合作的第三支单曲，收录于即将发行的EP《Desertropical》中，由哥斯达黎加独立厂牌Lácteo Cósmico发行。Dr. Rayo背后是智利-墨西哥裔打击乐手Red Jesus，现居马德里；Barzo则是来自圣何塞的DJ与制作人，曾remix过Janelle Monáe与Erykah Badu。歌曲以哥伦布的帆船、香蕉、可可、烟草等具有殖民与热带意象的词汇作为歌词核心，结合迷幻cumbia节奏，中速摇摆的贝斯线与现场打击乐构成骨架，电子制作层叠加于实录乐器之上。歌词强调对拉丁美洲根源的自豪感，提及的农作物早在哥伦布到来前便已生长于美洲大陆。整首作品在拉丁传统节奏与电子制作之间寻找平衡，是一首带有文化反思色彩的跨地域合作单曲。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A surprisingly-sophisticated and highly-entertaining album from a group of University of Illinois college students! Released on Brunswick Records in July of 1972.1. "The Monster Bride" (10:36) a very proggy, early King Crimson and Yes-like opening of bass, organ, clarinet, and delicate cymbal play turns in the second minute toward proggy brass rock--more like ELP meets BS&T. In the third minute the motif starts to smooth out before suddenly switching direction toward more light and playful circus music and then, in the fourth minute there is an equally sudden directional change toward more avant/eclectic Jazz-Rock Fusion before going Crimson and Zappa in the fifth. This is all quite tightly-performed and very sophisticated and unpredictable! It must have been something to compose and then pull off as a band in 1970s studio conditions. By the time we get to the end of the sixth minute everything slows down to a cymbal-supported droning organ for a Peter Hammill-like male vocal to enter and sing. Very Crimsonian! Flute and piano pick up from here with a very pretty, almost CHICAGO-like melody presentation and passage which builds and builds, horns entering and gathering forces over bass, guitar, and drum's rhythm track. At 5:22 everything stops for some percussion-backed dramatic very theatric narration of a sexually-piqued scene of the monster's reaction and response to the birth of his bride and child--which then leads to a finishing burst of CHICAGO-like brass rock. Very interesting! The sophistication of the compositions (and ability to pull it off in the studio) is the most impressive part. (18.375/20) 2. "Spiders (In Neals Basement)" (5:57) an accented male voice singing a sly lyric of film noir's detective-type music, like musical themes for scenes in a New Orleans juke joint or Chicago flop house. The music, performances both instrumentally and vocally are so colorful and spry. Great brassy theater music and great entertainment! Amazing that these were just a bunch of college kids! (9.333/10)3. "Witches Theme And Dance" (9:47) a brass rock song that opens like a LIGHTHOUSE song with great pace and energy before dropping down into a slow, plodding motif over which the gang issue some great four-part vocal harmony vocals. These guys must've done music theater or high school theater music. Bassist Neal Rosner is quite impressive (and, thankfully, placed forward in the mix), sounding a lot like Goblin or PFM's bassists. More stunning theatric stop-and-start composition performed with ease and professional precision over/within which electric guitar, voices, slide flute, and other mildly scary Hallowe'en noises contribute their solos and incidentals. Nice trilly flute solo in the final third--augmented by awesome "distant" flugelhorn. The finish is just perfect for the "lesson" of the witchy allegory. Another gem of a song; these guys are so creative and so talented! (18.875/20)4. "A Brief Message From Your Local Media" (9:59) here the band conjures up a four-part suite. It opens sounding like something from Aaron Copeland before organ, bass, hi-hat & bass drum lay down a soft carpet for a lone vocalist to begin his GREG LAKE-like "In the Court of the Crimson King" imitation. Obligatory flute joins in as "Greg" reaches his third verse--arpeggiated guitar chords and increasingly MICHAEL GILES-like drumming, as well. Around 4:30 there is a break in which narrator delivers a brief spoken-word summation of the contributions of Henry Ford to the workings of modern society, which is then followed by the development of a new motif of rather up-tempo organ- and flute-driven Jazz-Rock--which gains Latin elements in the eighth minute to give it a LEONARD BERNSTEIN West Side Story feel but then about a minute later the music moves more toward a pop/theatric-Brass Rock form similar to the snarky Hair, Godspel, and Pippen phenomenons. The music ends with a fading out calliope and military drums sound. Interesting. Though still delightfully creative and astonishingly sophisticated, the cohesiveness of this one is questionable (but, then, so is the flow of the typical radio or television programming!). (18.125/20) - a) "The Garden"- b) "The Assembly Line"- c) "Electric Man"- d) "Question"Total time 36:19Jazzy, brassy Crimsonian prog rock that sounds quite mature for a bunch of Illini students--and it's so entertaining, even addictive! Incredible for a debut album.A/five stars; a surprisingly-sophisticated and well-polished display of delightfully-entertaining compositions and performances. Who knew?! And, Whatever happened to?

items._cn_summary: 这张1972年专辑由伊利诺伊大学的学生乐团录制，展现出超出预期的成熟度与作曲技巧。曲目编排复杂多变，在前摇、爵士融合与铜管摇滚之间频繁切换，融合了ELP、King Crimson、Chicago等多重影响。单曲中可见戏剧性叙事段落、四部和声、笛与翼号的对话，编曲精密且富于即兴色彩。乐评逐曲详尽描述了动机转换、乐器编排与节奏段落，特别强调了贝斯手Neal Rosner的前置混音与酷似PFM/Goblin的低音线条。整体而言，作品在商业铜管摇滚框架内嵌入了相当多的前卫与融合元素，但本质仍偏向七十年代的爵士摇滚主流脉络，与纯粹的实验前卫或学院爵士路线存在一定距离。文章评论质量较高但内容被截断，信息略有不完整。

items.body: Depeche Mode, the English electronic band from Basildon, Essex, released “Some Great Reward” on 24 September 1984 through Mute Records. The album turns 42 this year. It was the band’s fourth studio album, and it reached number 5 on the UK Albums Chart and number 3 in West Germany. Most of the record was made in West Berlin. Sessions began at London’s Music Works studio and moved to Hansa Mischraum, where the band also mixed the album. Daniel Miller produced it with Depeche Mode and Gareth Jones, who had engineered the previous record and was promoted to co-producer here. The band carried over the sampling approach it had started on Depeche Mode’s ‘Construction Time Again’, building rhythms from struck metal and concrete rather than drum machines alone. Martin Gore wrote eight of the nine songs; Alan Wilder contributed “If You Want”, the last song he wrote for a Depeche Mode album. Dave Gahan sang lead throughout, with Gore taking the vocal on “Somebody”, recorded live with Wilder on piano. The nine-track album runs “Something to Do”, “Lie to Me”, “People Are People”, “It Doesn’t Matter”, “Stories of Old”, “Somebody”, “Master and Servant”, “If You Want” and “Blasphemous Rumours”. Mute had issued “People Are People” as the lead single on 12 March 1984, six months ahead of the album, followed by “Master and Servant” on 20 August 1984 and the “Blasphemous Rumours” / “Somebody” double A-side on 29 October 1984. Both later singles drew objections over their sexual and religious subject matter, and some radio stations declined to play “Master and Servant”. Brian Griffin photographed the sleeve at Round Oak Steelworks near Stourbridge, continuing the industrial imagery he and designer Martin Atkyns had used on the previous cover. The album title is a line from “Lie to Me”. The Some Great Reward Tour opened three days after release and ran to the end of July 1985, taking the band through the UK, Europe, North America and two shows behind the Iron Curtain, in Budapest on 23 July and Warsaw on 30 July 1985. The 14 December 1984 concert in Hamburg was filmed and issued as the band’s first live video, “The World We Live In and Live in Hamburg”. About Depeche Mode Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Dave Gahan and Andy Fletcher formed Depeche Mode in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, taking their name from a French fashion magazine. The band signed to Daniel Miller’s independent label Mute Records and released the synth-pop debut “Speak & Spell” in 1981. Clarke left after that album to form Yazoo with Alison Moyet, and Gore became the band’s main songwriter. Depeche Mode continued as a trio for “A Broken Frame” (1982), then expanded to a four-piece when Alan Wilder joined for “Construction Time Again” (1983), the album that brought sampled industrial sounds and Gareth Jones into the band’s productions. “Some Great Reward” extended that partnership and gave the band its first US chart single, “People Are People”, which reached number 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985 after a delayed run there. Mute followed the album with the compilation “The Singles 81>85” in October 1985, then “Black Celebration” (1986), “Music for the Masses” (1987) and “Violator” (1990), which produced “Personal Jesus” and “Enjoy the Silence”. Wilder left in 1995 after “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), and the remaining trio released “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013) and “Spirit” (2017). Fletcher died in May 2022. Gahan and Gore released “Memento Mori” as a duo in 2023 and toured behind it, documenting the Mexico City dates in the concert film “M”. Forty-two years on, “Some Great Reward” remains the point at which the Berlin sessions, the sampling and the leather-and-steel visual language settled into the form the band carried through the rest of the decade.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Depeche Mode第四张录音室专辑《Some Great Reward》发行42周年的纪念性回顾文章。专辑于1984年在伦敦与西柏林录制，制作人Daniel Miller与乐队及Gareth Jones共同完成。延续前作《Construction Time Again》的实验思路，放弃传统鼓机，转而敲击金属与混凝土采样构建节奏。Martin Gore撰写九首中的八首，Alan Wilder贡献了最后一首为乐队创作的曲目。唱片在英德两地榜单表现亮眼，主打单曲《People Are People》成为乐队最大商业突破，而《Master and Servant》与《Blasphemous Rumours》因性与宗教议题引发部分电台抵制。封面延续工业视觉主题，巡演横跨欧美并深入铁幕后的布达佩斯与华沙，留下首场官方实况影像。文章为信息性纪实文本，缺乏深度乐评分析。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐档案学者Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb等人组成的乐队录制，是其第五张作品。乐队从大量78转唱片中汲取灵感，使用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等形形色色的乐器进行演奏。27首短曲以Cravic近似法国香颂歌手Maurice Chevalier式的说唱演绎为主，融合了法国bal-musette、ragtime、jug band、香颂乃至skiffle等多种风格。部分曲目是对经典老歌的重新编排与致敬，包括向2020年去世的法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco的献礼作品。整张专辑以复古怀旧为基调，由一群多数年过七旬的乐手以严谨态度演绎被遗忘的音乐类型与风格，试图为这些古老素材注入新的活力与光彩。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场惨案（Peterloo Massacre）为题材，由Young 'Uns成员Sean Cooney创作原创歌曲，汇集吉他手Sam Carter、歌手Eliza Carthy、低音提琴手Ben Nicholls及兰开夏工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid共同演绎。专辑以书籍形式呈现，收录当时的信件、政治漫画与插图，构建多媒体体验。歌曲捕捉了集会现场的期待与兴奋、骑兵冲入后的恐惧与奔逃，以及事后的悲恸。Cooney的演唱具有说服力，三位歌手的声线交织形成丰富层次。在当下全球政府镇压抗议的背景下，这张作品既是历史回望，也是对现实的警示，音乐本身超越了文字记载，成为能够长久共鸣的歌曲集。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._genre: New Orleans R&B / funk / blues / jazz
items._cn_summary: 该专辑记录了Dr. John 1999年在德国Loreley露天剧场的现场演出，乐队由吉他、Bass和鼓手组成，以紧凑四重奏呈现新奥尔良传统。曲目涵盖新奥尔良经典如《Iko, Iko》、融合巫毒意象与放克节奏的《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》、Earl King的《Big Chief》等，展现了其作为新奥尔良音乐使者的多元面貌。演出被定位为一场融合经典与个人创作的Mardi Gras式综合秀，舞台设置与莱茵河的传说景观呼应。文笔侧重文化背景与现场氛围的描绘，对音乐本身的技术分析有限。作为德意志公共广播WDR旗下Rockpalast节目的档案发行，虽具历史价值，但从实验、前卫、爵士即兴等核心口味角度看，作品偏向传统根源音乐范畴，缺乏显著的跨界实验元素。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — The Science of the Seasons in 4 Points. Before discussing *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, Andrea Orlando's second album, it might be helpful to review the following preliminary points:1. The Bands. Andrea Orlando is the drummer on all four albums by La Coscienza Di Cena, an RPI band founded in Genoa in 2007, which released a superb self-titled debut album in 2011 and three other highly recommended albums between 2013 and 2018. Is it worth noting here that Genoa (Genova) is the birthplace of the illustrious PFM, one of the founding fathers of Italian progressive rock (RPI)?Before the formation of La Coscienza Di Cena, Andrea Orlando had already gained some recognition in this microcosm as a member of what it's fair to call the "Zuffanti nebula"?a transalpine prog music collective that began to coalesce around the Genoese bassist Fabio Zuffanti in the early '90s and gained greater visibility with Finisterre's debut album (1995).2. The Artist. Andrea Orlando joined Finisterre as early as 1997 on their *Live at Progday* and then on the fabulous *In Ogni Luogo* (1999), before returning for the 2019 comeback album. Orlando also played drums on *Mirrogames* (1998) by H�stsonaten, Zuffanti's other major band. In both cases, Orlando replaced Marco Cavani. To round out this overview, it's worth noting that drummer Andrea Orlando also contributed to the album by La Curva di Lesmo (2015), a duo that Zuffanti formed with Stefano Agnini, one of the two keyboardists on La Coscienza. And that brings us partially full circle.Let's now turn to the album itself by going over the other two points:3. The musicians. Since Andrea Orlando is one of the stalwarts of this famous Genoese music scene, it's no surprise that for his two solo albums, he called on other members of that same scene. For example, to give credit where credit is due, Zuffanti himself plays bass on one track from *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, and Boris Valle (Finisterre's longtime keyboardist) plays piano on another. Orlando, an accomplished drummer but also a capable keyboardist (with a predilection for the mellotron and organ), here cedes the piano parts?in addition to Valle?to Luca Scherani (H�stsonaten, La Coscienza di Zeno, La Curva di Lesmo) and to Agostino Marco (Finisterre, La Maschera, Zaal) for the Moog solos.On *Dalla Vita Autentica*, Andrea Orlando's previous solo album, the majority of the electric guitar parts were performed by two highly talented musicians: Marcella Arganese?who can be found in Ubi Maior and who regularly dazzles us with *Samura� of Prog*?and Laura Marsano, whom we've seen on Zuffanti's solo albums and those of drummer Maurizio Di Tollo. Two women on guitar?and not just any women?is rare enough to be worth noting, whatever the critics of "wokism" may say. On *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, Marcella has been replaced by Stefano Marelli, but Laura Marsano is always there to treat us to her poignant solos (the slow "Stagione Lontana"). The young singer Meghi Moschino contributes her calm, medium-toned voice to five of the seven tracks?a voice that reminds me a bit of Laura Mombrini's (Prowlers). On *Dalla Vita Autentica*, the robust vocals of Alessandro Corvaglia (another essential, ubiquitous figure on the RPI scene for several years), paired with those of Simona Angioloni (remember *Aries*, the band formed in the 2000s with? Zuffanti, him again), gave the whole a more robust feel. A matter of taste.4. The music. *La Scienza delle Stagioni* alternates between dynamic, vibrant tracks rooted in PFM's sun-drenched RPI, and tenderly romantic moments that unfold into expansive, emotionally charged symphonic prog, closer in style to *Hostsonaten*. By elegantly blending these two styles, the diptych "Il Sogno di Anastasia" (12:12) stands out as one of the album's most compelling tracks. In addition to "Il Sogno di Anastasia ? Parte Seconda," a lovely musical reverie with enchanting undertones, the album includes another instrumental, "City 40" (6:36), a sort of high-energy Latin version of "Samurai of Prog."The influence of Camel, noticeable from the very start of the previous album ("Le Forme Della Distanza"), is less pronounced throughout *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, giving way to more personal ideas, resulting in a kind of symphonic neo-prog with strong RPI influences. On the other hand, the extensive and frequent use of the mellotron (the long intro to "Stagione Lontana" with its celestial tones, or that of "La Strada del Ritorno," among others) draws the most serene moments toward the most ethereal Scandinavian prog.Of roughly similar length, the epic closing track, the highly symphonic "La Strada del Ritorno" (15:01), can be compared to the thrilling "Dalla Vita Autentica" (16:52), which closed the 2017 album of the same name, illuminated by an unforgettable solo by Marcella Arganese. But despite some structural and musical similarities, the comparison ultimately favors the latter, which is more ambitious and features more inspired melodies. Yet the melancholy that envelops the final section of "La Strada del Ritorno"?enhanced by Meghi's angelic voice and the serene appearance of the English and French horns?ultimately moves us, giving us the impression that a pale winter sun has come to breathe its loving breath upon us.At first glance, *La Scienza delle Stagioni* seems a little less striking than its predecessor, *Dalla Vita Autentica*. At the very least, it builds on its predecessor's strengths while retaining all its qualities, though without reaching quite the same heights. But let's not be fooled by first impressions. There are prog albums that possess a kind of natural clarity, made up of music whose beauty is immediately apparent; and others, like *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, that save their magic for a little later, revealing it just after we've finished listening, when we think we've moved on to something else. But that is the secret art of these mysterious works: to prepare for us an immediate future more beautiful than expected. *La Scienza delle Stagioni* possesses that special magic that fairies bestow as they lean over the cradle of certain works?a magic that stays with you and illuminates your path long after the notes have faded away.

items.body: Review by Matti — Today is the official release date of the third album by Confusion Field, the Finnish heavy prog act sovereignly led by multi-instrumentalist, vocalist, composer and producer Tomi Kankainen. This time he plays himself all of the guitars as well, and the drums are now played by an Italian session drummer, Martino Malacrida. I have reviewed both of the earlier albums (dating from 2021 and 2023), and, given that I'm not an active listener or connoisseur of the heavier genres, I struggle a bit to find something new to say. But I certainly still feel Confusion Field makes "modern Finnish heavy prog at its best". If you have enjoyed CF before, you will have a great listening with this one too, or if you're new to the band, let's say that if you are into contemporary heavy/metal prog and bands such as Riverside and Porcupine Tree, you may be happily surprised. The moods are rather dark but not too depressive. The sound is very well produced and balanced. The guitars have the metallic bite but they don't go TOO far into aggressiveness for me to digest. The synths are incorporated into the meaty but clear texture, even though there may be slightly more of them than before. Malacrida is an excellent metal oriented drummer. No gun machine attacks but an intelligent sense of the whole. And what's best, Kankainen has an excellent voice quite comparable to Mariusz Duda of Riverside. This is something I cannot say very often within heavier end of prog. He never growls or yells at the top of his lungs and yet he has no difficulties whatsoever to convince the listener.The songs feel pretty tight at the average five minute length. All compositions sound fine and well crafted. Perhaps they aren't very distinctive from each other, in the progressive sense, but I don't get the feeling of tiresome sameness. The closing piece is the longest (7:16) and especially here the synths, a bit reminiscent of the mid-80's Simple Minds (Sparkle in the Rain, New Gold Dream), really make a nice extra dimension to the powerful soundscape. An album well worth checking out!
items._genre: heavy prog / progressive metal / modern prog
items._cn_summary: Confusion Field 来自芬兰，由多乐器手 Tomi Kankainen 主导，第三张专辑《Resilience Remains》邀请意大利鼓手 Martino Malacrida 参与录制。Kankainen 包揽所有吉他声部，合成器被更显著地融入厚重的器乐织体，嗓音沉稳，接近 Riverside 主唱 Mariusz Duda 的质感，乐评特别指出这一点在该流派中较为难得。整体氛围偏暗但不压抑，吉他带有金属质感却未过度激进，鼓手风格注重整体结构感而非炫技。歌曲平均约五分钟，末曲时长七分钟余，合成器段落令人联想到八十年代中期的 Simple Minds。乐评认为各曲编排扎实但彼此辨识度有限，属于该类型爱好者会满意、但难以给实验或前卫口味听众带来太多意外的制作。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是吉他与颤音琴的二重奏组合，由Ralph Towner与Gary Burton合作演出。原作者起初对吉他与颤音琴的搭配抱有疑虑，担心流于平淡，然而实际聆听后发现这是一张令人惊艳的月度佳作。整张专辑呈现出精致细腻的室内爵士气质，两位演奏者在原声乐器上展开充分对话，旋律线条舒展，和声层次丰富。作为1986年的录音，作品体现了ECM厂牌典型的北欧式爵士美学——克制、抒情、注重空间感。乐评虽短，但肯定了这种编制下出人意料的艺术表现力，证明简约的乐器配置同样能承载深度的音乐表达。

items.body: Conscience, the German electropop and synthpop project of Rüdiger Illg, releases the compilation “Uncharted Vol. 1 (The Singles 2009-2023)” on Echozone on 25 September 2026. It gathers Conscience’s single releases from that period into one set, adds one new song and three new mixes, and presents every track remastered. The label describes a second volume, “Uncharted Vol. 2”, as already in the works. Despite the plural billing Echozone sometimes gives the project, Conscience remains a one-man operation: Illg writes, plays and produces every track himself at Science2, his home studio in Leeste, Lower Saxony. He formed Conscience in 1991, but “Uncharted Vol. 1” starts its clock at 2009, not at the project’s founding. Echozone explains why: Conscience did not sign a record deal until 1998, with the “Hardware” EP, and that contract proved short-lived. Illg then signed to Echozone, whose own account of the compilation dates that move to around 2008, when “Theatre Of Deception” served as the lead single for the album “Gravity Has Gone”; Side-Line’s earlier research into the project’s Echozone catalogue had put that signing a year later, in 2009. Physical releases stopped soon after over cost, and for years Conscience issued albums and EPs with no accompanying singles at all. That changed with the 2020 album “Sentient”, after which every Conscience album has carried multiple single releases, the run “Uncharted Vol. 1” now compiles. The compilation follows the single “Explain Everything”, which Echozone issued on 28 August 2026 as an advance taste of the same collection. About Conscience Rüdiger Illg founded Conscience in August 1991, working first with a single Yamaha SY22 synthesizer, and has written, played and produced every track since under that name at Science2. He also records as Science O.C.N. and Chaos Network. The project’s first six years produced cassette-only releases traded through the tape network, followed by a first CD in 1998 and a run of CD-Rs through the early 2000s. NewEx Records picked up Conscience in 2007, and Illg signed to Echozone in 2009, a relationship that has produced the bulk of the catalogue since, including the albums “Phases³” (2025) and “Suspended In Time” (2026) and the singles and EPs “Uncharted Vol. 1” now draws its selections from. Guest vocalists across the catalogue have included Colin Angus of The Shamen and Dan Söderqvist of Twice a Man. “Uncharted Vol. 1 (The Singles 2009-2023)” is Conscience’s first compilation to collect that stretch of the catalogue in one release, with a second volume already planned.
items._cn_summary: 这是德国单人项目Conscience（主脑Rüdiger Illg）即将发行的单曲合辑，将2009至2023年间在Echozone厂牌下发行的作品集结重制，并附加一首新曲与三首新混音。文章以信息发布为主线，详尽交代了厂牌签约沿革、实体发行中断的缘由，以及从2020年专辑起恢复单曲发行的转变过程。文字侧重时间线与行政细节，几乎未涉及音乐本身的音色质感、编曲手法或美学立场。对暗潮/电子受众而言，仅能从中获得作品集合的发行信息与Rüdiger Illg自1991年起坚持一人包办创作演奏制作的工作方式概览，缺乏可供聆听的审美判断依据。

items.body: Demonwarp released “Viral Empire” on Re:Mission Entertainment on 25 September 2026. The album is Demonwarp’s third full-length, running ten original tracks of industrial and EBM rhythm work layered with dark synth and metal-edged electronics, its lyrics turning on surveillance, corruption, artificial intelligence and resistance to power. Viral Empire by Demonwarp Two tracks were released as singles ahead of the album: “Protocol Obey” and “Spreading The Flames.” “Viral Empire” adds three remixes of those singles to close out its thirteen-track sequence: Frontal Boundary reworks “Protocol Obey,” while Dawn Of Ashes and Dread Risks each contribute separate versions of “Spreading The Flames.” Demonwarp handled all production and vocals on the album; Kristof Bathory mastered it, and KGM Studio supplied the cover art. Pre-orders opened on 4 September ahead of the 25 September release. The first pressing is a limited run of 100 digipak CDs, alongside the full digital release on Bandcamp. “Viral Empire” follows 2024’s “Dominion,” Demonwarp’s second album, which featured Jenna Cogan on vocals. About Demonwarp Demonwarp began self-releasing music in 2022 with the single “Devil’s Sunset” and the ten-track album “In The Night,” followed the same year by the singles “Relent” and “Lust Lies In Betrayal.” Further self-released singles, “Just Ashes,” “Scream At The Gates,” “Onikiri” and “Fading Flesh,” followed through 2023. Demonwarp’s second album, “Dominion,” arrived in September 2024 with Jenna Cogan featured on vocals. “Viral Empire,” Demonwarp’s third full-length, arrived on 25 September 2026 through Re:Mission Entertainment, preceded by the singles “Protocol Obey” and “Spreading The Flames” and the remixes of both that close the new album.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是对Demonwarp第三张全长专辑《Viral Empire》的资讯性发布，内容涵盖发行日期、曲目数、混音版本及制作人员信息。专辑以工业和EBM节拍为基础，叠加暗色合成器与金属质感电子音色，歌词涉及监控、腐败、人工智能与权力抵抗等主题。除两首先行单曲的三首混音外，还发行了限量100张的D-pack CD及Bandcamp数字版。文章本质上是厂牌发行通告，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论、声音设计分析或艺术价值评估，信息密度低且重复内容较多。作为适合该用户口味的作品方向，但文字为纯新闻稿性质，无评论深度支撑，因此评分受限。

items.body: 今週も世界中の最新ジャズニュースから気になるトピックをピックアップ。 サックスという楽器が抱えてきた振れ幅を、今週は何度も思い出させられる。コルトレーン生誕100年の節目、ブランフォード・マルサリスとダイアン・リーヴスの共演、ローランド・カーク晩年の実験、そしてアンディ・シェパードとジョーイ・アレクサンダーの新作。世代も国籍も異なる5つの動きを追う。 ブランフォード・マルサリスとダイアン・リーヴス、Blue Noteでの再会 ブランフォード・マルサリス・カルテットと、ヴォーカリストのダイアン・リーヴスによるコラボレーションアルバム『Dedicated To You』が、Blue Noteからリリースされた（UK Vibe誌のレビュー）。出典で確認できるのはブラックヴァイナル仕様と限定カラー盤の存在までで、CDでの発売については出典本文に記載がないため、ここでは触れない。 ブランフォードは、弟ウィントン・マルサリスと並び称されてきたソプラノ／テナー奏者で、2002年作『Footsteps of Our Fathers』でジョン・コルトレーンの『A Love Supreme』を完全収録した経緯を持つ人物でもある。一方のダイアン・リーヴスは、10代の頃にクラーク・テリーからスタンダード・レパートリーの手ほどきを受け、1977年には「カルデラ」への参加を経て、1987年にBlue Noteと契約した最初の歌手となった歌い手である。系譜の異なる二人が同じ盤の上で言葉を交わす構図に、このアルバムの聴きどころがある。 出典：https://ukvibe.org/album_reviews/branford-marsalis-dianne-reeves ローランド・カーク、晩年の「新しさへの追求」 マルチリード奏者ローランド・カークの晩年の意欲作『Slightly Latin』が、Jazz Journal誌のコラム「JJ 09/66」で改めて取り上げられている。トロンボーン奏者ギャレット・ブラウンとの共同編成のもと、ラテン音楽の要素を取り込み、カーク特有の角ばった音色をより柔らかく響かせようとした一枚だという。 本作の背景には、1960年代半ばのジャズシーンにラテン音楽の語彙が浸透していった時期の空気がある。カークがバリトン・サックスという新たな声を得ようとしていたことも、Jazz Journalの評は伝えている。同誌はこの模索を「新しさへの絶えない追求」と評した。   出典：https://jazzjournal.co.uk/2026/09/20/jj-09-66-roland-kirk-slightly-latin アンディ・シェパード、静謐に寄せる5作目 イギリスのサックス奏者アンディ・シェパードの5作目となる新作『Salt Catchers』が、ECMから発表された（UK Jazz News）。出典によれば、本作は伝統に根ざした叙情性と、音数を絞った静けさを湛えた一枚だという。 シェパードは、ピアニストのリタ・マルコトゥッリ、ベーシストのミシェル・ベニータら長年の共演者と再びこの一枚を作り上げた。出典によれば、シェパード自身はキャラ・ブレイの「Lawns」をこれまでライブでは演奏してきたが録音してこなかったといい、今回初めて本作で録音に収めたという逸話も紹介されている。ここでは、シェパード個人がこの叙情性とどう向き合ってきたかという、小さな一点に絞って触れておく。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/andy-sheppard-salt-catchers ジョーイ・アレクサンダー、10歳で世界に見出された歩み ジャズピアニスト、ジョーイ・アレクサンダーを取り上げた評論記事が『UK Jazz News』に掲載された。バリ島出身の彼は、2014年、10歳でニューヨークに移り住んだ直後にその演奏がウィントン・マルサリスの目に留まり、そこから国際的なジャズシーンへ足を踏み入れた経歴を持つ。 「アジア発のジャズプレイヤーが国際的に認識される時代」という大きな見立てを、今回の出典1件だけで裏づけるのは難しい。ここでは、一人のピアニストがどこから歩き出し、誰に見出されたかという個人史の線を辿るに留める。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/joey-alexander コルトレーン生誕100年の節目に ジョン・コルトレーンが生まれてから、今年で100年になる。NPRのジャズ評論欄では、この節目に寄せた論考が公開されている（NPR、2026年9月22日）。 今回参照できた素材は表題と概要のみで、論考本文の具体的な主張までは確認できていない。テナー・サックス奏者としての革新性については、出典本文を確認できた段階で改めて扱いたい。 出典：https://www.npr.org/2026/09/22/nx-s1-5976887/marking-the-100th-birthday-of-jazz-great-john-coltrane 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY ／今週の話題まとめ】コルトレーン生誕100年、そしてブランフォードとリーヴスの邂逅ほか は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — What starts out sounding like a Funk-Jazz outing of the highest quality seems to turn taward the R&B, Disco, Black Dance, and even Adult Contemporary/Smooth Jazz charts. But then we are only getting started: soon we find ourselves treated to one absolutely amazing journey through Power Fusion of the highest caliber. 1. "Master Funk" (3:42) Al is playin' it all on this (not really, but a lot of the tracks!) There is a Brothers Johnson-meets-Billy Preston-and-The Hues Corporation feel to this one. Whereas the song feels a bit like a one-trick pony novelty song, there are definitely some praise-worthy elements to the music: these funk masters are definitely talented! (8.875/10)2. "Baker's Daughter" (5:34) the quartet takes a long route to introducing the full structure of this one, using wah-wah-ed "underwater" funk bass, ample cymbals and drums, broad keyboard swaths, and treated soprano saxophone to introduce the sound palette over an extraordinary two minutes time before Al power drums his way into establishing the pace and power of the Smooth Power Fusion. Stu and Welton kind of hold space trying to keep up with Al's frenetic pace while Gary seems to take great satisfaction on delivering his Jerome Richardson-like melodic soprano sax solo over the top. Stu gets some solo time in the fourth minute for his piano, Chick Corea-style, as Al's drumming keeps pushing, pushing, and pushing. Great performances from Al, Gary, and Stu; I just wish Welton had a little more room and confidence to spread his wings a little. (9/10)3. "Come into My Life" (5:10) a sensual, ARP Odyssey strings-rich opening that is marred a bit by and "out-of-place" chunky & forward bass. Stu is playing some nice grand piano as Al handles drums lite and the Odyssey and Gary belts it out like a castrati with his soprano sax. Nice and relaxing, even appropriate for those late night date-ending "drinks" that couples resort to in order to warm-up and commit to sexual interplay. (8.875/10)4. "Nyctophobia" (7:00) finally we get some Stanley-Clarke/Jaco Pastorius-level bass play from Welton Gite! They're off to the races for this one with Gary Bartz plying his skills with ease on his soprano sax. As much as I usually dislike this particular instrument, I have to admit that Gary makes it sound like a walk in the park (and I know it's not!) If I had to walk through scary dangerous street-alleys in the dark of the late night, the intrepid spirit that Gary displays with his soprano sax is the kind of fearless courage I would want at my side (or coursing through my veins). Stu's MiniMoog solo in the sixth and seventh minutes takes that instrument to extremes that no one, not even Jan Hammer or Chick Corea, ever took it! Everybody's performance on this piece is jaw-dropping--and they keep it going for all of its seven minutes. (14.75/15)5. "Virtue" (8:23) a drumming clinic in which Al seems to be playing a medium-paced straight-time rhythm track but his tom-tom and cymbals cry out for forgiveness as they are so mercilessly (though almost lackidaisically) abused! Though Fender Rhodes is the first instrument to join (and try to match Alphonse's energy), it's Stu's grand piano and Gary's alto sax that the listener soon finds each screaming out "hard bop" Jazz. Meanwhile, Welton's bass is being beaten silly like it's on a DOUG ROUCH or PERCY JONES outing. In the fourth minute Stu's electric piano begins flying all over--through a complete review of the Herbie-Chick lexicon. And then there's the MiniMoog-dominated sixth minute: exhibiting yet another "outside the box" display of synth creativity. This is Power Fusion at its absolute best, folks! (19/20)6. "Poobli" (5:30) Smooth Jazz with a funk-cool vibe reminiscent of some of Earth, Wind & Fire's most groovin' dance tunes--all thanks to Welton and Al's cool, ultra-laid back rhythm track and Stu's dreamy Fender Rhodes play in the middle. Gary's plays some mean and unusual tenor sax lines to toy with the main melody lines, later retweeted by Al's ARP Odyssey strings and Stu's MiniMoog--which Gary must see as a challenge to his manhood as he takes off into new and extraordinary heights. Why this guy isn't a household name when it comes to discussing saxophone players I do not know! He may be the one that makes me finally appreciate, even like, the saxophone! (9.333/10)"The Mouzon Drum Suite" (8:31) : (18.21/20) = 9.10 - 7. a) "Jazz-Rock-Improvisation" (2:23) solo drumming . . . with effects. (4.425/5) - 8. b) "Out of the Desert" (1:45) steady simple, metronomic drumming with lots of percussion instruments played and over the top--especially the ones that bend and twist pitch. (4.333/5) - 9. c) "Colors of Africa" (2:39) gong opening followed by kalimba, marimba, twizzles, shakers, cymbals, and hand drums of all shapes, sizes, and elements (clay, wood, metal)--plus kit drums and true African chant vocals! Awesome! (5/5) - 10. d) "Total Swing" (1:44) virtuosic display at the traps. Sped up at the end. (4.45/5)Total Time: 43:50Al is a drummer who at first did not impress me as much as the other "greats" but, over time I've come to experience and appreciate both his skills and his creative talent as well as his commendable abilities beyond the drum kit and percussion trunk. He has, here, created a truly marvelous masterpiece of fully-developed and fleshed-out Jazz-Rock Fusion.A/five stars; a veritable masterpiece of eclectic Jazz-Rock Fusion--one that centers fully in the domain of the Power Fusionists. HIGHLY recommended.

items._cn_summary: 这张1977年的专辑由鼓手Alphonse Mouzon领衔，融合了放克、迪斯科、节奏布鲁斯与力量型爵士融合元素。评论指出专辑前半部分偏向商业化的放克和R&B风格，如首曲带有Brothers Johnson式的舞池律动；第三曲以ARP Odyssey合成器弦乐和柔美的高音萨克斯营造性感氛围。然而后半部分展现了更深的音乐实力，第四曲中贝斯手Welton Gite展现出Stanley Clarke级别的技巧，高音萨克斯和MiniMoog合成器的极限运用令人印象深刻。第五曲则是Mouzon的鼓技展示。整体来看，专辑虽然演奏水准高超，尤其是鼓、贝斯和高音萨克斯的表现值得称道，但其音乐取向更偏向70年代商业化爵士融合和放克舞曲路线，与实验前卫和学术爵士的口味存在明显距离。

items.body: Tanner McGraw sings and John Beckmann stays off the microphone on “Nothing Is Missing”, the third single from Utopia PKWY, out on 25 September 2026 with a video. Utopia PKWY is the new project of Beckmann, the New York songwriter and producer behind The Mortal Prophets, and the single precedes the project’s first album, “Debut”, due on 6 November 2026. Beckmann wrote and produced the track alone; McGraw takes the lead vocal and Lawson Mars adds backing vocals. Utopia PKWY mix post-pop hooks with synth-wave-tinged psychedelia, and bring keyboards, theremins and sitars into the arrangements. The single follows “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”, released on 3 July 2026, and “Sleep In Moving Colors”, released on 14 August 2026, both with official videos on the project’s YouTube channel. The “Nothing Is Missing” video was not yet public at the time of writing, so the player below carries the second single, whose video upload is titled “I Sleep In Moving Colors”. Beckmann described the new song as “Less a song than a philosophical hallucination, more like a midnight transmission from the far side of grief – where loss doesn’t disappear, it simply changes frequency and keeps humming beneath the skin.” The project takes its name from Utopia Parkway in Queens, the street where the Surrealist artist Joseph Cornell lived and worked. Beckmann calls McGraw and Mars, his two younger collaborators, the “kids in the neighborhood”. Both singers already appeared on the two most recent psychedelic dream-pop albums by The Mortal Prophets, and Utopia PKWY moves that line-up into brighter, more melodic songs. ‘Debut’ tracklist and release dates “Debut” runs to ten tracks: “I Knew You Were Trouble”, “Sleep In Moving Colors”, “Nothing Is Missing”, “If I Could Steal One More Kiss”, “You Talk Like Every Feeling”, “What Disappears”, “Come In Waves”, “Glitter And Doom”, “Fall Into You” and “Dreaming I’m A Rock Star”. The tracklist spells the opener “I Knew You Were Trouble”, while the single and its video carry the title “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”. The closing title also appears on The Mortal Prophets’ July 2026 album “Ain’t No Fool”. The earlier Utopia PKWY singles are on Spotify and Apple Music; the album page on the official site lists the release dates for all three singles and the album. About Utopia PKWY Utopia PKWY is the 2026 side project of John Beckmann, a New York singer, songwriter, producer and visual artist who has recorded as The Mortal Prophets since 2022. That project opened with the EP “Stomp The Devil” on 8 July 2022 and the album “Me And The Devil” on 9 December 2022, both built on reworked blues standards. “Dealey Plaza Blues” followed on 28 July 2023, the ambient guitar album “Guitarworks” on 22 December 2023, the EP “Sleeping In My Bed” on 15 March 2024, the opera “Hanussen: The Enigmatic Clairvoyant” on 15 April 2024, the EP “ICNCLST/” on 20 August 2024 and “Laurel Canyon – Lost Sessions (1966-69)” on 29 November 2024. In 2025 came “Ghost Land” (17 January), “French Summer” (16 May), “Guitarworks II” (28 July) and the covers EP “Under The Influence” (5 December). The move toward dream-pop and psychedelia began with “Hide Inside The Moon”, released on 2 January 2026, the first Mortal Prophets record with Tanner McGraw on lead vocals. “Not Here, Not There” followed on 3 April 2026 with McGraw and Lawson Mars sharing the vocals over synth-wave keyboards, theremins and sitars, and “Ain’t No Fool”, with Jake Burden on vocals, arrived on 3 July 2026. On the same day Beckmann launched Utopia PKWY with “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”, again with McGraw and Mars singing, and released “Sleep In Moving Colors” on 14 August 2026. “Nothing Is Missing” on 25 September 2026 is the last single before “Debut” on 6 November 2026.
items._cn_summary: Utopia PKWY是纽约音乐人John Beckmann在2026年开启的全新侧项目，延续其The Mortal Prophets时期的创作脉络。乐队将后流行旋律钩子与合成器浪潮元素相融合，并在编曲中引入特雷门琴、西塔琴、键盘等乐器，营造出迷幻而明亮的音色质感。第三支单曲由主唱Tanner McGraw担纲，Lawson Mars提供和声，作品被Beckmann描述为带有哲学幻觉色彩的概念表达。专辑共收录十首曲目，整体从psychedelic dream-pop向更明亮、更具旋律性的方向过渡。项目名取自皇后区Utopia Parkway——超现实主义艺术家Joseph Cornell曾在此居住与创作。原文为资讯类新闻稿，缺乏深度乐评分析。

items.body: Boston gothic post-punk and deathrock band Gossip Collar has released “Eaten of Worms”, its third full-length album, on September 4, 2026 through Bat-Cave Productions. The ten-track record is available on CD and LP through the label, with a digital edition on Bandcamp. Eaten Of Worms by Gossip Collar ‘Eaten of Worms’ tracklist and credits Eaten of Worms was recorded and mixed by Marc Valois at Dead Moon Audio in Somerville, Massachusetts, and mastered by Jeff Lipton at Peerless Mastering in Boston. The album’s ten tracks are: Disguise My Heart Scavengers Big Top Comes Crashing Down Haerisis Dead Thing Why Me? Peaceful In Daylight Spelling Misery Unsafe State Merchants Of The Wave The record pairs electronic textures with serrated guitar work, running through recurring images of water, predatory animals and religious dread across its ten songs. CD and LP copies can be ordered directly through Bat-Cave Productions, with a download code included. About Gossip Collar Gossip Collar formed in Boston in the dark basement scene at the tail end of the pandemic, bringing together members previously involved with The Showcase Showdown, Spitzz and Secret Hearts. The band’s lineup is Victoria on vocals and guitar, Tom on guitar, Mark on bass and Megan on drums. Gossip Collar released a self-titled debut album on April 7, 2023, followed by spinning silk for parasites on October 31, 2024. Eaten of Worms, out September 4, 2026 via Bat-Cave Productions, is the band’s third album. Gossip Collar has performed alongside The March Violets, Pink Turns Blue, Rendez-Vous, Haunt Me, House of Harm, Fotocrime and Sympathy Flowers. Eaten of Worms extends that catalogue with the band’s most recent studio work to date. Follow Gossip Collar: – Bandcamp – Instagram

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: In September 1827, Hector Berlioz saw the actress Harriet Smithson play Ophelia in a Paris production of Hamlet and fell hopelessly in love. When his letters went unanswered, he turned the obsession into music, completing a symphony in 1830 at the age of twenty-six. It was first performed at the Paris Conservatoire that December, without Smithson in the audience. She heard the revised work two years later, and in 1833 the two were married. The program follows a young artist through five scenes: a reverie, a ball, a day in the country, a march to his own execution and a witches’ sabbath. The last two are opium nightmares, and the woman he loves haunts every scene as a recurring melody, the idée fixe. In the finale her theme returns as a cackling parody on a shrill E-flat clarinet, and bells toll as the Dies irae rises from the depths of the orchestra. Recordings part company on the details: the repeats in the first movement and the march, the optional cornet in the waltz, the bells, and old instruments versus modern. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the 10 best recordings of Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique. Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Colin Davis Colin Davis gives the listener the whole score: Every repeat is observed, the march’s among them, and the waltz includes the optional cornet part. Davis tightens the drama one movement at a time, and even Berlioz’s oddest sonorities are made to count. The price is a certain restraint. The ball ends in good order rather than a whirl, and the last two movements are held on a tighter leash than the music invites. Complete and played with unbroken concentration, this 1974 recording is the natural place to start. Davis Amazon Presto Apple Boston Symphony Orchestra, Charles Munch Where Davis builds the symphony with steady care, Munch plays it as theater, and this 1962 recording is a touchstone for that raw intensity. The first three movements are ardent, but the real storm is saved for the last two. When it breaks, the march and the witches’ sabbath erupt in a frenzy that still startles, with the whole orchestra driven to the edge. His faster 1954 recording is fiercer still in places, but finer playing and sound tip the balance toward the later version. For Berlioz at his wildest, this is the one to hear. Munch Amazon Presto Apple Orchestre Révolutionnaire et Romantique, John Eliot Gardiner John Eliot Gardiner took his period orchestra into the hall where the symphony was first heard in 1830. He seated the musicians as their counterparts sat in that era, with the violins split left and right, and the 1991 recording still sounds like a discovery. It flows more easily than the period-instrument pioneer before it, and its dynamics stretch from a bare whisper to full force without the inner lines ever blurring. Both repeats are taken, and the optional cornet brightens the waltz. The dry room leaves little halo around the sound, and it is no more thrilling than the great modern-orchestra versions. What it offers instead is the orchestra Berlioz knew, in the very room where his symphony was born. Gardiner Amazon Presto Apple Paris Conservatoire Orchestra, Ataúlfo Argenta Every movement runs faster than usual in Ataúlfo Argenta’s 1957 recording, and the scenes cut past like a film reel run too fast. Argenta skips the first movement’s repeat but takes the march’s, and the playing is not always polished, with some unevenness in the brass. None of that dims the impetuous energy, which carries the whole symphony along like one long, breathless dream. Argenta Amazon Presto Apple French National Radio Orchestra, Thomas Beecham A shadow lengthens through this famous 1959 recording. Beecham takes the story entirely seriously, and his march to the scaffold starts slower than usual, so the threat builds before the procession picks up speed. It is a darker, more measured journey than Argenta’s headlong dash. Beecham leaves out the first-movement repeat, and his mono recording from two years earlier burns hotter. Yet the slow build here pays off in a witches’ sabbath that is truly chilling. Beecham Amazon Presto Apple Orchestre National de France, Leonard Bernstein Every mood swing in the score is played to the full in this 1976 recording. Leonard Bernstein drives the first movement hard, yet he means every one of its quiet, hymn-like closing chords. The waltz has a teasing charm, and the idée fixe drifts through it and is gone. The march to the scaffold is the core of it, a procession that moves the listener to pity. Bernstein’s first New York recording has a sharper edge, and the sound here lacks some depth, but the performance wears its heart openly from first bar to last. Bernstein Amazon Presto Apple Cleveland Orchestra, Pierre Boulez Here the symphony is heard, above all, as a symphony. Pierre Boulez keeps close to the composer’s tempo markings, and the shape of each movement stands out with rare clarity. The Cleveland Orchestra plays superbly, with gorgeous strings and every climax held in firm control, and the disc adds Tristia with the orchestra’s chorus. Compared with Munch, this is a cool performance that keeps its emotional distance from the story. What this 1996 recording offers instead is Berlioz’s design laid out in full view. Boulez Amazon Presto Apple Rotterdam Philharmonic Orchestra, Yannick Nézet-Séguin This 2010 recording turns the drama inward. If Munch’s Berlioz is a fever, Yannick Nézet-Séguin’s is a confession, with the story told from inside the artist’s head as memory and feeling. The country scene is gently drawn, and the distant thunder at its close is kept low. The march stays in proportion, and in the finale the horrors are more dreamed than seen. Anyone after theatrical terror should look elsewhere, but the searching, personal tone is the point, and the disc adds La mort de Cléopâtre, sung by Anna Caterina Antonacci. Nézet-Séguin Amazon Presto Apple Les Siècles, François-Xavier Roth Nearly three decades after John Eliot Gardiner’s period-instrument version, François-Xavier Roth and Les Siècles bring the instruments of Berlioz’s day back to this score, and daylight falls between the lines. Roth went back to the composer’s manuscript before recording, and he lets each episode breathe before the next begins. The country scene is spare and unhurried, its period oboe and cor anglais calling to each other in their own reedy colors. In the witches’ sabbath, the bells come from La Côte-Saint-André, where Berlioz was born. The textures trade weight for light, and the finale closes in with a steady tread rather than an explosion. This 2019 recording is a beautifully observed performance, with every page freshly considered. Roth Amazon Presto Apple San Francisco Symphony, Michael Tilson Thomas From its opening bars, Michael Tilson Thomas’s 1997 recording shows the San Francisco Symphony in dazzling form, its playing at once exact and impassioned. The slow country scene never drags, and the march swings between the hushed and the enormous. For all that power, the last two movements burn less fiercely than the first three. The disc adds two excerpts from Lélio, Berlioz’s sequel to the symphony, and a 2024 remaster brings the recording to Apple Music in Dolby Atmos. items.body: Mesh will release the mini-album “Fallen Angel” on Dependent Records on 27 November 2026. The British duo of Mark Hockings and Richard Silverthorn describe the nine-track record as an addendum to this year’s album “The Truth Doesn’t Matter” rather than the start of a new chapter, built from songs that grew out of writing sessions the pair started after touring behind that record. The label had asked for a fourth single from “The Truth Doesn’t Matter”; Hockings and Silverthorn instead wrote enough new material for close to half an album of additional songs. “Fallen Angel” combines four newly written tracks with remixes and a live recording, offering what the band calls a deeper dive into the themes of “The Truth Doesn’t Matter”. Pre-orders for “Fallen Angel” open on 24 September, the same day the mini-album’s fourth single from that campaign, “Trying to Save You”, arrives on streaming platforms in a mix by Olaf Wollschläger. The title track follows as a single on 21 October with a new music video featuring the band, ahead of the full CD and vinyl release on 27 November. The tracklist: Fallen Angel Protect Your Neck Not This Time The Meeting of the Broken Tilt Trying to Save You (single mix) The Truth Doesn’t Matter (live, recorded on this tour) Fallen Angel (extended version) Trying to Save You (remix) “Fallen Angel”, “Protect Your Neck”, “Not This Time” and “The Meeting of the Broken” are entirely new songs; “Tilt” receives its first physical release. Mark Hockings and Richard Silverthorn wrote and recorded all tracks and produced the mini-album with Vaughn George on live keyboards and Sean Suleman on live drums; it was recorded at Mesh HQ and The Summerhouse in Bristol, mixed by Olaf Wollschläger and Mesh at Cottonbeat Studio in Burscheid, Germany, with additional mastering by Wollschläger. Mark Hockings supplied the artwork and photography, with additional artwork, editing and layout by Nico Janse van Rensburg. “Fallen Angel” will be released as a jewel case CD, a limited clear vinyl LP capped at 500 copies, and a standard black vinyl LP; the CD and a KitAlbum Tour Edition will be available at Mesh’s live shows roughly six weeks ahead of the wider release. Distribution runs through SPKR. At least two of the new songs will be played live starting with Mesh’s show in Krefeld, Germany, on 1 October. The band’s confirmed live dates through November: 1 October 2026 – Krefeld, Germany – Kulturfabrik 2 October 2026 – Braunschweig, Germany – Westand 3 October 2026 – Dresden, Germany – Reithalle Strasse E 4 October 2026 – Berlin, Germany – Kesselhaus 5 November 2026 – Łódź, Poland – Klub Scenografia 6 November 2026 – Halle/Saale, Germany – Capitol 7 November 2026 – Liberec, Czech Republic – Dům Kultury Liberec (Sever Synth Festival) Hockings and Silverthorn also confirmed that “Looking Skyward” is set to return on red vinyl “very, very soon”, and that “Who Watches Over Me?” will receive a 25th-anniversary reissue in 2027 as an art book edition with refreshed artwork, following the return of its rights from Sony Music; that album will also return to streaming platforms next year. The details emerged during a Zoom Q&A with Hockings and Silverthorn on 22 September, which Mesh had previously teased as previewing an “unusual release”. About Mesh Mesh formed in 1991 in the UK when vocalist and guitarist Mark Hockings and keyboard player and vocalist Richard Silverthorn began writing together, later joined by keyboardist Neil Taylor. The band released the “Fragile” EP in 1994 and its debut album, “In This Place Forever”, in 1996, followed by “The Point at Which It Falls Apart” in 1999, reissued in a 25th-anniversary edition in 2024. The major-label release “Who Watches Over Me?” in 2002 widened the band’s European audience, especially in Germany, and 2006’s “We Collide” was produced with former Depeche Mode collaborator Gareth Jones. “Automation Baby” (2013) reached number 33 on the German album chart, and “Looking Skyward” (2016) climbed to number 12 there. Mesh continued as the core duo of Hockings and Silverthorn, touring with drummer Sean Suleman and additional live keyboard players, and added Vaughn George to the live lineup in April 2023. Hockings also records solo as Blackcarburning, releasing the album “Watching Sleepers” and the EP “Divide Us”. Mesh’s most recent album, “The Truth Doesn’t Matter”, arrived in 2026 on Dependent Records, preceded by the singles “Exile”, “Hey Stranger” and “This World” and followed by a European tour; “Fallen Angel”, out 27 November 2026, extends that album cycle with new songs, remixes and a live recording.

items.body:
The sweeping soundtrack for The Violinist has arrived.

Released by Milan Records on 25 September, The Violinist (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) features music by Singaporean composer and Golden Horse winner Ricky Ho and Spanish composer Isabel Latorre. The pair co-wrote the original score for the Annecy-winning animated film, bringing together Eastern and Western musical traditions across 29 tracks.

Featuring intimate violin melodies and sweeping orchestral themes, the score accompanies a story centred on friendship, memory, resilience, and hope. Among its tracks are 'The Pursuit', 'First Duet', 'Sunset Sonata', 'Fall of Singapore', 'A New Sunrise', and 'Strings of a Distant Heart'.

The Violinist spans Singapore and Malaya from the early 20th century through the Japanese Occupation. The film follows two childhood friends brought together by music as war, displacement, and the passage of time reshape their lives.

Produced by Robot Playground Media, The Violinist is an official co-production with Spain's TV ON Producciones and Italy's Altri Occhi, with worldwide sales handled by France tv distribution.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

-

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是为动画电影《The Violinist》创作的原创配乐，由新加坡作曲家 Ricky Ho 与西班牙作曲家 Isabel Latorre 联合创作，共收录 29 首曲目。配乐以小提琴旋律为核心，配合管弦乐编制展开，融合东西方音乐传统。曲目包括《The Pursuit》《First Duet》《Sunset Sonata》《Fall of Singapore》《A New Sunrise》等，主题围绕友谊、记忆、坚韧与希望。电影背景跨越二十世纪初的新加坡与马来亚，叙事聚焦战争与流离中因音乐结缘的两位童年挚友。该配乐由 Milan Records 发行，定位为动画电影的商业配乐项目，制作层面属于国际合作，作曲手法偏向传统电影配乐框架。整体内容偏向新闻稿性质，缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析与创新性探讨。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — The odd title for this difficult third album is somewhat reflected in the content, which, while still emphasizing skilled acoustic interplay, has seen its Celtic edge gone dull, and with it most of the earlier spark. The band seems to be channeling a theatrical FAIRPORT or MELLOW CANDLE, though a less committed ISB, SIROGYRA or JAN DUKES DE GRAY might be more a propos, or even a disoriented Lindisfarne as seen on a few contemporaneous albums, but without that group's prior success as a triggering event. It's like a live performance of new material in which jamming and vocalise fill in overly busy and inauthentically complex arrangements. One of the big misses is the inclusion of the unsubtle "Don't Forget the Animal" phrasing on 3 tracks, a theme handled better, though well short of masterfully, on a full length bonus track available with the group's debut. Still, "Is it Me" carries on the understated folk of its predecessors while POLLY BOLTON's best vocal contribution to date is in the ballad "I Heard Somewhere", combining with Martin Jenkins on-point violin. Overall though, this is a dispirited effort that fits the band about as well as the wrong pantaloons.
items._genre: prog folk / acoustic / british folk rock
items._cn_summary: Dando Shaft的第三张专辑延续了民谣摇滚路线，但评论指出其凯尔特锋芒已钝，失去了前两张的火花。专辑被比作戏剧化的Fairport或Mellow Candle，也像少了投入感的Steeleye Span。在声学器乐交织的基础上，歌曲编排过于繁复，缺乏真实感，即兴填充显得冗长。专辑最明显的失败之处在于三首歌曲中重复出现'Don't Forget the Animal'的主题，处理生硬。不过'Is it Me'延续了前作的低调民谣风格，叙事曲'I Heard Somewhere'则展现了Polly Bolton最佳的人声表现，与Martin Jenkins精准的小提琴配合。总体而言，这是一张让乐队失去方向感的作品，如同标题暗示的穿错了裤子。
